newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-NYMEX futures to grind out further gains.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-NYMEX futures to grind out further gains.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20

* Whether the market can take off again depends largely on a particular fundamental influence today, the APIs. The uptrend of the market is still holding, but only just. * Yesterday's technical factors were knocked out of line due to unexpected fundamental news, but the inverted Head and Shoulders pattern is still friendly towards gasoline in the short term.

The uptrends for NYMEX crude and product futures remain intact for the time being with technical indicators pointing out a slow route to higher ground but the impetus from gasoline is slowing with the recent market leader, running out of steam, analysts said.

"Gasoline virtually negated the reverse head and shoulders formation that some participants were looking towards on Monday, but the recovery before the close may have given the bulls mild encouragement." Leslie Nicholas at GNI Research said.
"Whether the market can take off again depends largely on a particular fundamental influence today, the APIs. The uptrend of the market is still holding, but only just," Nicholas said.

"Tom James at Credit Lyonnais Rouse in Singapore said, "Yesterday's technical factors were knocked out of line due to unexpected fundamental news, but the inverted Head and Shoulders pattern is still friendly towards gasoline in the short term".
"Enough not to wish to sell in the short term," he added.

Nicholas points out a couple of converging trendlines on the spot month continuation chart stemming from the 71 cent high of July 1 and the August 12 low of 61.40 cents that come in today at 64.75 and 66.50 cents, as a guideline to the trend.
This trading pattern is drawing a flag or pennant formation on the spot month chart which is usually read as a continuation signal of the current trend.

Moving averages, are also mildly supportive for gasoline with the market managing to close above the 10 and 20-day measures. Slow stochastics, on the September chart crossed bearishly at a high level on Monday but the contract stood a little firmer in ACCESS trade.

Monday's price action for WTI left a hammer formation on the spot month continuation chart which according to Japanese candlestick charting techniques coming in the downtrend of the past three-days could flag a return to higher ground, or at least it puts a good base in the market at around $19.90.

ACCESS trading saw the contract holding just above $20 on the spot month chart but still below the short term uptrend line from the August 8 low of $19.49 which also forms the base of a flag formation which normally signals the continuation of a trend.
The September contract chart shows a similar pattern but here prices are holding above the longer term trendline stemming from the June 15 $18.50 trough and touches on the August 8 low of $19.49.
Heating oil's slow rise was checked on Monday when it ended below uptrend support but it has good double bottom support around 54.25 cents from last week and momentum indicators offer room for gains.
